pr.title: Call a request's set-aside action dismiss request
pr.head: 17e38e6d0c431fe7e1739c634ab681a1c7fb6fbc

summary: Projector's panel lists the items agents post to your inbox: questions, notices, and requests, where a request is work only you can do, such as testing a build. Opening an item shows its drawer, a list of actions, each pressed by a digit. Digit 8 sets an item aside: dismiss question and dismiss notice for those kinds, and, until this change, decline request for a request.

"Decline" reads as a refusal, which is stronger than what pressing it usually means. This pull request renames the action to dismiss request, so every kind of item uses the same word on the same digit. The recorded outcome stays the same. The button now runs project inbox dismiss in place of project inbox decline, and the CLI has always recorded a dismissed request as declined. So the agent that posted the request still hears DECLINED, and a dismissed request's drawer still says Declined and offers restore request on 8.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:

  • The pull request body says the panel no longer runs decline. It still runs it for a prompt that says Declined; only the drawer action goes away.

groups.title: The drawer's dismiss action
groups.kicker: One action, named dismiss, for every kind of item
intro: The drawer builds its actions in register.tsx. Before this change, a request's set-aside action took a special name, decline, so its key, label, and command all read decline. Now every open item gets the same dismiss action on 8, labeled with the item's kind, and act, the function that runs an inbox command for the panel, no longer takes decline.
The tests check the new label and command, and that dismissing a request records it declined.

checks.text: In a scratch inbox store, project inbox dismiss and project inbox decline with no text each store a request's answer as {dismissed: true, declined: true}, and each one's deliverer sends DECLINED. A dismiss has declined a request since requests first shipped in #372.

files.note: Drops the request-only setAside name, so the drawer's 8 action is dismiss for every kind of item.

checks.text: The panel still runs project inbox decline elsewhere, when you send a prompt that quotes a request with a plain Declined under it. Only the drawer's action stops using it.

files.note: Expects dismiss request on 8, the inbox dismiss command, and a declined record.

checks.text: Run against the base's register.tsx, three of these tests fail, so they catch the old label and command. The full suite passes at this head: 180 pass, 0 fail.
The test's name, at line 1936, still says the drawer offers "no dismiss", while this line asserts dismiss:1 8 dismiss request. Rename it so it says the drawer offers discuss, dismiss, and snooze.

groups.title: The panel's documentation
intro: The plugin guide's panel section now names dismiss request wherever it named decline request, and the keyboard list says 8 presses dismiss or restore, with no request-only exception.

files.note: Renames the request's action in the drawer, start-action, act-at-once, and keyboard paragraphs.

checks.text: The keyboard bullet still says "Dismiss asks to be sure" on 8 8. That holds only for a pull request; an item's dismiss acts at once, as this file says above. The sentence predates this change.
